verdict.label: GFX1151_BLOCKED_OFFICIAL_EP_ARTIFACT
verdict.statement: the OS catalog offers no execution provider at all on this host and no official AMD GPU EP artifact is published for it; therefore the AMDGPU EP can be neither installed nor registered, and no GPU execution claim is made

hypotheses.statement: The Windows ML 2.x API/SDK surface is broken or too old, so the catalog cannot list providers.
evidence: reports/experiment_b/CATALOG_PROBE.json (S_OK create + S_OK enum, three repeats)
reports/experiment_b/CATALOG_SURFACE_MATRIX.json (5 usable surfaces, all 0 providers, incl. official 2.5.96)
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: a surface returning S_OK with >=1 provider, or an HRESULT failure

hypotheses.statement: The ExecutionProviderCatalog serves no EP entry to this device, so there is nothing to ensure_ready.
evidence: reports/experiment_b/MSIX_INVENTORY.json:deployment_events (0 AMD.GPU events; workload machinery active for the NPU EP)
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: a catalog listing AMDGPUExecutionProvider with ReadyState=NotPresent on this host

hypotheses.statement: The AMD GPU EP MSIX/DLL is not installed and no DLL exists anywhere on the host.
evidence: reports/experiment_b/NEGATIVE_TESTS.json (registering a missing DLL fails with a DLL_LOAD_ERROR)
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: the package appearing in HKLM AppxAllUserStore or an amdgpu-ep.dll being found

hypotheses.statement: The HP OEM display driver blocks the AMD GPU EP (Adrenalin minimum not met, or OEM packaging unsupported).
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: an AMD/HP statement mapping 32.0.22018.5 to an Adrenalin version, or the EP loading on this driver

hypotheses.statement: gfx1151 kernels/operators are unsupported by the AMD GPU EP build.
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: an AMDGPU EP DLL on this host plus a kernel-level session failure, or an official gfx list

hypotheses.statement: An AMDGPU request appears to succeed while running on CPU, so a green result is not proof.
hypotheses.what_would_settle_it: n/a - this is a measurement hazard, mitigation is the get_providers() + profiler assertion

answers.q1_can_amdgpu_register_and_execute_on_80: NO - not on this host today. The provider is not offered by the catalog and the EP package/DLL is absent, so there is nothing to register.
answers.q2_exact_stage_where_it_stops: S2/S3: the ExecutionProviderCatalog enumerates zero providers (S_OK), so ensure_ready cannot be addressed and no artifact is installed (S4/S5).
answers.q3_direct_evidence_for_that_stage: CATALOG_PROBE.json / STANDALONE_CATALOG.json (3/3 stable, HRESULT 0x00000000, 0 providers), CATALOG_SURFACE_MATRIX.json (6 usable surfaces, all 0), MSIX_INVENTORY.json (absent in HKCU + HKLM scopes, 0 AMD.GPU deployment events), PROVISIONING_ATTEMPT.json.
answers.q4_excluded_causes: Windows ML API/SDK breakage (H1: refuted), Python-projection artifact (6 surfaces), missing shared runtime/OS version (both MET), Store-side acquisition failure (no Store errors recorded), unprivileged-enumeration error (registry cross-check).
answers.q5_causes_still_without_evidence: H4 HP OEM driver incompatibility (Adrenalin version not derivable), H5 gfx1151 kernel/operator coverage (no EP to test), and the exact reason the Store/WU targeting does not offer the AMD GPU EP package to this DID.
answers.q6_what_microsoft_amd_must_supply: Either (a) publish/target the AMD GPU EP MSIX (Microsoft.WinML.AMD.GPU.EP.Framework.*) to DID 0x1586 via the Store/WU channel so the catalog lists it, or (b) publish an official signed redistributable of onnxruntime-ep-amdgpu with a supported gfx list and driver requirement; plus a statement of which Adrenalin version corresponds to OEM WDDM 32.0.22018.5.
answers.q7_how_to_upgrade_from_blocked_to_gpu_go: The moment the catalog lists AMDGPUExecutionProvider with ReadyState=NotPresent: ensure_ready -> verify amdgpu-ep.dll hash -> register -> run the AMDGPU canary with AMDGPU profiler nodes > 0, CPU nodes = 0, by-name numeric parity and a PT task oracle PASS -> strict receipt verifier ALL_OK.
